title: SENSE in Practice: Quantifying the End-to-End Benefits of Intent-Based Bandwidth Reservation for Exascale Science Workflows
problem: Scientific workflows across multiple administrative domains lack deterministic, secure, and orchestrated network services; data movement relies on best-effort approaches causing unpredictable performance
motivation: Exascale science increasingly requires coordinated resource sharing across institutional boundaries. Networks must provide deterministic, priority-aware services rather than best-effort delivery to meet data-intensive scientific requirements.
method: Software-Defined Networking for End-to-end Networked Science at the Exascale (SENSE) using intent-based networking and multi-domain orchestration; evaluation on comprehensive testbed including GNA-G AutoGOLE, NRP, FABRIC, and LHC CMS production infrastructure
key_novelty: First practical evaluation of intent-based bandwidth reservation across multiple administrative domains for exascale scientific workflows, demonstrating network as first-class schedulable resource
contributions: Intent-based service requests successfully translated to network configurations
Average provisioning times: 183 seconds for simple services, 290 seconds for complex multi-domain workflows
Demonstration that SENSE maintains guaranteed bandwidth allocations
Higher-priority data flows complete significantly faster than best-effort scenarios
Network positioned as first-class schedulable resource for scientific computing
limitations: Specific performance improvements quantified in abstract limited to provisioning times; detailed comparison with best-effort scenarios not shown; scalability to larger network domains unclear
primary_theme: Intelligent Network Infrastructure for Exascale Science
